title: Search Element in Array
statement:
Write a function that searches for a `target` element in an array of integers `nums`.

If the element is found, return its 0-based index. If the element is not present in the array, return `-1`.

examples.explanation: Target 6 is not in the array, so we return -1.

editorial.approach: Scan the array from index 0 to n - 1. If any element matches target, return index, otherwise return -1 after the loop.

hints: You can iterate through the array using a loop.
For each element, compare it with the target value.
If they match, return the current loop index. If the loop ends without matching, return -1.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Using JavaScript's built-in `indexOf` method which searches the array sequentially.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Implement manual linear search by looping over the indices of the array, comparing `nums[i]` with target, and returning `i` immediately upon finding the target.

interviewExplanation: Linear search is the simplest search algorithm. We iterate through the array of size `n` and compare each element to the target. It runs in O(n) worst-case time (when target is at the end or not present) and O(1) space.
